title: Drum lessons with Mr. MacMillan across the ward line
summary: In Houston he took lessons from a teacher in Fifth Ward, riding the streetcar with his drum, and learned to read music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Oh, yeah, well, I took lessons in Houston, when I was staying in fourth ward. I had to go to fifth ward for this music teacher.
Oh?
Mr. MacMillan was the name.
Oh?
And I had to ride the streetcar. See, now they didn't allow fourth ward guys over in fifth ward. They didn't [allow it either.]
Honestly?
If they knew about it, there would be a big fight going on. It was just like that/.
Really? Yeah.

But I would go from fourth ward to fifth ward, on the streetcar, with my drum under my arm. And in the time I'd have to go was when school let out. So they must have figured I lived in fifth ward or something like that.
Yeah.
And -- but I never had any trouble, none whatsoever in going from fourth to fifth ward.
Because your drum might have come to harm if you had.
Oh, that's what I was worried about.
Yeah.
Because I wasn't afraid of anybody, really.
No, no.
Because any time a fight started, it was all right with me. But I didn't want nobody to hurt my drums.
Yeah, right.
Everybody seemed to like it, one of those things.
Isn't that funny?
And they never did ask me where I lived. They wanted to know where I was going, because I was going to take my music lessons, one of those things.
That's funny.
So I learned how to read in Houston, Texas.
Oh, that was very good. So you didn't have to be afraid of the music at all.
No, no.
Because then, plus what you learned in the Glee Club --
I didn't get afraid of music until I got to be grown.
Enough to know what was lacking.
That's right, oh, yes.
